snippet.textDisplay: Yes my 87 year old mom got early dementia and things were getting bad. They put her on Memantine and in 1 month it’s like a miracle! Her mind is sooo much better and her personality is back after 2 months on 1/2 dose! I feel like I have my mom back. No more paranoia. She finally agreed to getting a POA. She had been fighting me on that, but once her mind was more rational she understood the importance.  I don’t know how long it will last but it’s suppose to slow down the disease. I’m counting my blessings❤

snippet.textDisplay:
Yes, it is consuming. It is harder than other things to me. It’s been at lease 5 years, but my Mom broke both femurs and hips within less than 3 years. She has osteoporosis. My husband built her a tiny house right near our dining room. We wanted to give her privacy but also have her near in case she needs us. It was hard traveling to go take care of her during those times she was hospitalized and recovering at home. Her friends finally talked her into moving with me and my husband.

Also, I have Lyme. My health is difficult, and have to rely on my daughter and my husband to help me. Also, Mom gets bossy and tries to tell me what to do. 🙈 Between my health, taking care of the needs of my family, and my Mom, it definitely is a challenge. I think it’s definitely important to rely on others to support you whether you have good health or not. Stay strong!💚🙏🏼💪🏽

snippet.textDisplay: My grandma, 93yrs old, is going through some major gaps but hasn't been diagnosed w dementia or alzheimer's. She's been very independent & capable. Her long-term memory is on point 👌 ...but her short-term is shot🤪👈! I'm 42 & help my dad, her son who is 72yrs old, w her. It's getting worse as time goes on. Forgetfulness.  Frustrations. Blood pressure issues & lack of taking medication. Thankfully not falling but she has passed out from extreme heat exhaustion twice in 5 yrs. It's stressful to say the least. My dad & I take turns taking her to doctor appointments & checking up on her daily.  I believe we are to honor our parents & grandparents as long as we're healthy & able.  They took care of us when we were helpless & vulnerable.  It's our turn to give back. ❤️‍🩹

snippet.textDisplay: We all have to plan for this. When's my mom showed increasing dependence on me for medical care, I recommended that we both sell ou single homes and buy a duplex. That allowed us independence and security. In  my mom's last years, We were able to use her long-term care insurance for day activities and care and I was there the remaining 16 hours. That was a practical solution. Every time you create a plan, the requirements will change. Be flexible. Be strong. Be loving. Be caring. And find a way to educate the medical community about dementia in an emergency situation. And please know we have to find every way to prevent our own selves from early dementia. Take care of yourselves

snippet.textDisplay: I’m 65. We just did two months of home hospice for my dad who passed soon after he turned 90. It was grueling, but it felt like a privilege. One minute he was fine the next minute he fell. He didn’t hurt himself, but he was paralyzed. We found out a week before he passed That he had liver cancer, kidney cancer, and bile duct cancer. My mom is going to be 89 in December. She has a defibrillator and a pacemaker and she is still driving. She is sharp. I think she would be less weak though if she had been on hormones. I haven’t had hormones yet. I have an appointment with the doctor that is listed as one of the people I need to seek for hormone replacement. I just went to a lecture she gave, and I was very impressed. Anyways, my sister lives in the same state as my mother and my beautiful mother is pretty independent and pretty happy living alone, but she misses my father. The doctor said that he could give her medicine and she could live another 10 years and she said no I’m ready to go join my husband and my son. I don’t know what the next couple of years will look like, but we work as well as we can as a family and we have nieces and nephews to help us. We had a team of 15 when my dad was in home hospice and we all shared duties. I was the nurse, dispensing the medicines and wiping him when he went to the bathroom, I’m strong enough to lift him. I wish my mom had taken hormones so that she wouldn’t be so real and she wouldn’t be so tiny at 100 pounds. I think she would want to live more years. I am thrilled to have you as a reference as I make a health journey that will hopefully make my Childrens future with me much easier and more fun. Both my parents were sharp till the end for my dad and still for my mom, so I’m very hopeful that I will have my full cognitive ability.
